| Page | What it does |
|---|---|
| [basic-auth](https://hono.dev/docs/middleware/builtin/basic-auth) | Protects routes with HTTP Basic Authentication (username and password). |
| [bearer-auth](https://hono.dev/docs/middleware/builtin/bearer-auth) | Authenticates requests using a bearer token in the `Authorization` header. |
| [body-limit](https://hono.dev/docs/middleware/builtin/body-limit) | Rejects requests whose body is larger than a size you set. |
| [cache](https://hono.dev/docs/middleware/builtin/cache) | Caches responses using the Web Cache API (for example on Cloudflare Workers or Deno). |
| [combine](https://hono.dev/docs/middleware/builtin/combine) | Combines several middleware into one, using helpers like `some`, `every` and `except`. |
| [compress](https://hono.dev/docs/middleware/builtin/compress) | Compresses response bodies with gzip or deflate. |
| [context-storage](https://hono.dev/docs/middleware/builtin/context-storage) | Stores the request `Context` in `AsyncLocalStorage` so you can read it outside handlers with `getContext()`. |
| [cors](https://hono.dev/docs/middleware/builtin/cors) | Adds Cross-Origin Resource Sharing headers and handles preflight requests. |
| [csrf](https://hono.dev/docs/middleware/builtin/csrf) | Guards against CSRF attacks by checking the request's origin and content type. |
| [etag](https://hono.dev/docs/middleware/builtin/etag) | Adds ETag headers and returns 304 Not Modified for conditional requests. |
| [ip-restriction](https://hono.dev/docs/middleware/builtin/ip-restriction) | Allows or blocks requests based on the client IP address or range. |
| [jsx-renderer](https://hono.dev/docs/middleware/builtin/jsx-renderer) | Lets you set a JSX layout and render pages through `c.render()`. |
| [jwk](https://hono.dev/docs/middleware/builtin/jwk) | Verifies JWTs against a JSON Web Key set, which can be fetched from a remote JWKS URL. |
| [jwt](https://hono.dev/docs/middleware/builtin/jwt) | Verifies JSON Web Tokens and rejects requests without a valid one. |
| [logger](https://hono.dev/docs/middleware/builtin/logger) | Logs each request and response with its method, path, status and elapsed time. |
| [language](https://hono.dev/docs/middleware/builtin/language) | Detects the user's language from the query string, cookie or `Accept-Language` header. |
| [method-not-allowed](https://hono.dev/docs/middleware/builtin/method-not-allowed) | Returns 405 Method Not Allowed when a path matches a route but not the HTTP method. |
| [method-override](https://hono.dev/docs/middleware/builtin/method-override) | Lets a request override its HTTP method, for example a form POST acting as PUT or DELETE. |
| [mount](https://hono.dev/docs/middleware/builtin/mount) | Mounts another framework's fetch-style app (any handler that takes a `Request`) under a path prefix. |
| [pretty-json](https://hono.dev/docs/middleware/builtin/pretty-json) | Pretty-prints JSON responses when the request includes `?pretty`. |
| [request-id](https://hono.dev/docs/middleware/builtin/request-id) | Generates a unique ID for each request and sets it in a response header. |
| [secure-headers](https://hono.dev/docs/middleware/builtin/secure-headers) | Sets security headers such as CSP, HSTS and X-Frame-Options, similar to Helmet. |
| [timeout](https://hono.dev/docs/middleware/builtin/timeout) | Aborts a request with a timeout error if the handler runs longer than a set time. |
| [timing](https://hono.dev/docs/middleware/builtin/timing) | Adds `Server-Timing` headers so you can see timing metrics in browser dev tools. |
| [trailing-slash](https://hono.dev/docs/middleware/builtin/trailing-slash) | Redirects URLs to add or remove the trailing slash. |

The same sidebar links to `/docs/middleware/third-party`, which is outside the built-in section.

These formatter options are named in those pages:

- `line-length`: maximum line width (shared with the linter). Formatted code may still exceed it in some cases.
- `quote-style`: preferred quote character for strings, e.g. `"single"`. The default is double.
- `indent-style`: spaces or tabs, e.g. `"tab"`.
- `docstring-code-format`: opt-in formatting of Python code examples inside docstrings. It covers doctest, Markdown fenced blocks, and reStructuredText literal blocks and `code-block` directives.
- `docstring-code-line-length`: line-length limit for those docstring examples. The default is `dynamic`, which follows the surrounding code's `line-length`. A fixed number also works.
- `preview`: opts into preview-style formatting changes, such as the fluent layout for method chains.
- `nested-string-quote-style`: how quotes are chosen for nested strings in f-strings. `"preferred"` reuses the configured quote style when targeting Python 3.12+.

Two related settings appear but aren't formatter options:

- `extend-exclude` is a general setting. The page uses it to stop Markdown files from being formatted.
- `# fmt: off` / `# fmt: on` / `# fmt: skip` are comment-based suppression, not configuration.

The page says Ruff "does not currently expose any other configuration options" beyond these. It points to the Settings page for the full list. That page is outside `/ruff/formatter/`, so I didn't read it. Options like `line-ending` and `skip-magic-trailing-comma` aren't mentioned anywhere in the pages I read.

**Vercel gives more bandwidth on its free tier.**

- **Vercel (Hobby plan):** 100 GB/month of Fast Data Transfer is included. Hobby has hard usage caps, and you can't buy extra.
- **Netlify (Free plan):** There's no fixed bandwidth allowance. The plan has a 300 credit/month hard limit shared across production deploys, compute, web requests and bandwidth. Bandwidth costs 20 credits per GB, so the most you could get is 300 ÷ 20 = **15 GB/month**. That's only if you used nothing else. Each production deploy costs 15 credits, and requests and compute also draw from the same pool, so real-world bandwidth will be lower.

Vercel's 100 GB is about 6–7 times Netlify's theoretical 15 GB maximum, and the gap is larger once you count Netlify's other credit costs.

Both pages were scraped fresh today. Vercel also meters other items separately, such as 1M CDN requests/month on Hobby. Netlify's free plan is hard-capped and can't incur charges. Vercel's Hobby plan is also limited to personal, non-commercial use.

The latest release in the changelog is **uv 0.13.2**, released 2026-10-19. I read the raw `CHANGELOG.md` rather than the GitHub page. Its sections are:

**Enhancements**
- `uv workspace metadata` now reports all installed packages, including ones outside the selected resolution.
- Exporting `pylock.toml` now includes supported environment restrictions.
- Dropped GET and HEAD requests are retried when fetching package and index data.
- Encoding declarations are preserved in wheel data scripts that need shell launchers.
- `uv python find --script` now shows causes and hints when it can't find an interpreter, including with `-q`.
- ksh activation instructions are now valid, and non-relocatable environments work under OpenBSD-derived ksh.
- uv-build's `[build-system].requires` validation now allows PEP 508 direct URLs, including Mercurial and extensionless archive URLs.

**Python**
- Added PyPy 3.11.17 and 3.12.15.

**Preview features**
- With `wheel-variants`, uv now fetches and parses PEP 825 index-level variant metadata.

**Performance**
- Complex dependency markers no longer cause exponential work when simplified, traversed or exported. They also use less time and memory to parse and store.
- The resolver uses less memory on large dependency graphs, forks, extras and dependency groups.
- Project discovery is faster in large workspaces because member names are cached.
- The uv and `uv-build` binaries are smaller, CycloneDX exports are faster, and TOML parsing allocates less.

**Bug fixes**
- `--exclude-newer` is now respected when a newer wheel for the selected source distribution is already cached.
- URL credentials no longer leak through diagnostics or persisted metadata.
- Signed `--find-links` URLs that differ only in sensitive query values now get separate cache entries.
- PEP 751 environment restrictions are honored when installing or syncing from `pylock.toml`.
- `uv publish` uses configured credentials before prompting, and doesn't prompt when nothing is uploaded.
- Recursive build globs match complete file paths, and invalid license symlinks are ignored.
- Invalid `uv pip compile --python-version` values and invalid `pylock.toml` output filenames now return errors instead of panicking.
- Repeated resolution conflicts involving fixed-priority packages no longer panic.
- Version aliases are created correctly when installing managed Python into a relative directory.
- `uv pip check` shows incompatibilities with `-q`.
- Logically equivalent dependency markers compare as equal regardless of construction order.

There is also a **Rust API** section. It starts with a requirement to enable the `unsafe-url` feature to use raw `url::Url` APIs in `uv-pep508`. I only read the first 5,000 characters of the file, so that section is cut off and I haven't seen the rest of it.

- **v24 Krypton:** it became LTS on 2025-10-28 and moves from Active LTS to Maintenance LTS on 2026-10-20, tomorrow. After that it gets only critical fixes and security patches, until 2028-04-30.
- **v22 Jod:** it is in Maintenance LTS and reaches end of life on 2027-04-30.
- **v26:** it is scheduled to become LTS on 2026-10-28, nine days from now. When it does, it will be the newest LTS line. Its end of life is 2029-04-30.

For a new project today, v24 is the right choice. After 2026-10-28 you could use v26 instead.

The crawl only returned 2 pages (the formatter overview and the Black-compatibility page), so I didn't reach the 15-page cap. The overview page is the one that documents options. The docs say Ruff "does not currently expose any other configuration options" beyond these.

**Options named on the formatter page**
- `line-length`: sets the line width. The example uses 100, and the page says Black also supports this option.
- `quote-style`: picks the quote style. The example uses `"single"`.
- `indent-style`: picks spaces or tabs. The example uses `"tab"`.
- `line-ending`: sets the line endings. The page only mentions it in prose ("unlike Black, it does support configuring… line endings"), with no example or description.
- `docstring-code-format`: turns on formatting of Python code examples in docstrings. It's opt-in.
- `docstring-code-line-length`: sets the line limit for those docstring examples. The default is `dynamic`, which follows the surrounding code's `line-length`. You can also set a fixed number, and the example uses 20.
- `extension`: maps extra file extensions to Markdown so they get formatted, for example `{ mdx = "markdown", qmd = "markdown" }`. This is a general Ruff setting, not a `[format]` one, but the page uses it for Markdown formatting.
- `extend-exclude`: this is also a general setting. The page uses `extend-exclude = ["*.md"]` to switch off Markdown formatting.

**CLI**
- `ruff format --check` reports unformatted files and exits non-zero without writing changes.
- `ruff format --help` lists the full set of CLI options. The page doesn't list them.

**Other formatter controls**
- `# fmt: on`, `# fmt: off` and `# fmt: skip` pragma comments suppress formatting.
- In Markdown, `<!-- fmt:off -->` and `<!-- fmt:on -->` skip code blocks. The blacken-docs equivalents also work.

The page links to the Settings reference (`/ruff/settings/#format`) for the full list of format settings. That page is outside `/ruff/formatter`, so I didn't crawl it. The black page and the lint-conflict section didn't add any more options.

- **Current conditions:** it is clear (WMO code 0) and 14.6 °C. The next three days are overcast (code 3), dry and mild.
- **Time:** "current" is as of 00:30 on 2026-10-20, Lisbon local time. That is already the next calendar day for you, so the forecast starts on the 20th.

**Vercel's free tier gives more bandwidth.**

- **Vercel (Hobby):** 100 GB/month of Fast Data Transfer. The scraped text doesn't label the column for that line, so I read it as the Hobby figure. Please confirm it on the live page.
- **Netlify (Free):** no fixed bandwidth allowance. The plan has a 300-credit monthly limit, and bandwidth costs 20 credits per GB. Even if you spent every credit on bandwidth, that's at most **15 GB/month**. Production deploys (15 credits each) and compute draw from the same credits, so real bandwidth would be lower.

So Vercel offers about 100 GB against Netlify's 15 GB ceiling, roughly 6–7× more.

Sources: https://vercel.com/pricing and https://www.netlify.com/pricing/ (scraped just now).

The latest release in the changelog is **uv 0.13.2**, released 2026-10-19. I read the raw `CHANGELOG.md` rather than the GitHub page. I only read the first part of the file, so the Rust API section at the end of this release is cut off and not covered here.

**Enhancements**
- `uv workspace metadata` now reports all installed packages, including ones outside the selected resolution.
- Exported `pylock.toml` files now include supported environment restrictions.
- Dropped GET and HEAD requests are retried when fetching package and index data.
- Encoding declarations are preserved in wheel data scripts that need shell launchers.
- `uv python find --script` shows causes and hints when it can't find an interpreter, including with `-q`.
- Activation instructions are now correct for ksh, and non-relocatable environments work under OpenBSD-derived ksh.
- uv-build's `[build-system].requires` validation now allows PEP 508 direct URLs, including Mercurial and extensionless archive URLs.

**Python**
- PyPy 3.11.17 and 3.12.15 were added.

**Preview features**
- `wheel-variants` now fetches and parses PEP 825 index-level variant metadata.

**Performance**
- Complex dependency markers no longer cause exponential work when simplified, traversed or exported.
- Parsing and storing complex markers takes less time and memory.
- The resolver uses less memory on large dependency graphs, forks, extras and dependency groups.
- Project discovery is faster in large workspaces because member names are cached.
- The uv and `uv-build` binaries are smaller, CycloneDX exports are faster, and TOML parsing allocates less.

**Bug fixes**
- `--exclude-newer` is respected when a newer wheel for the selected source distribution is already cached.
- URL credentials no longer leak through diagnostics or persisted metadata.
- Signed `--find-links` URLs that differ only in sensitive query values now get separate cache entries.
- PEP 751 environment restrictions are honored when installing or syncing from `pylock.toml`.
- `uv publish` uses configured credentials before prompting, and doesn't prompt when nothing is uploaded.
- Recursive build globs match complete file paths, and invalid license symlinks are ignored.
- Invalid `uv pip compile --python-version` values and invalid `pylock.toml` output filenames now return errors instead of panicking.
- Repeated resolution conflicts involving fixed-priority packages no longer panic.
- Managed Python installed into a relative directory now gets its version aliases created correctly.
- `uv pip check -q` shows incompatibilities when it fails.
- Logically equivalent dependency markers are treated as equal regardless of construction order.

**Node.js 24 ("Krypton") is the current LTS. It gets security updates until April 30, 2028.**

- **Active LTS:** v24 is in Active LTS until about October 20, 2026, which is tomorrow. After that it moves to Maintenance LTS, which only gets critical bug fixes and security patches. The latest release is 24.22.0, from October 14, 2026.
- **Security updates end:** v24 reaches end of life on April 30, 2028.
- **Node.js 26:** v26 is the Current line today. It is scheduled to become LTS on October 28, 2026, and to reach end of life on April 30, 2029.
- **Node.js 22:** v22 ("Jod") is in Maintenance LTS until April 30, 2027.
- **Node.js 20:** v20 reached end of life on April 30, 2026, so it no longer gets security fixes.

Sources: the official [Node.js release schedule](https://github.com/nodejs/Release/blob/main/schedule.json), [nodejs.org previous releases](https://nodejs.org/en/about/previous-releases) and [endoflife.date/nodejs](https://endoflife.date/nodejs).
